newsitem.title: GERMANY: German consumer electronics sales to rise - ZVEI.
newsitem.headline: German consumer electronics sales to rise - ZVEI.

text.p: Sales of German household electrical products will pick up in the second half of 1997 after a slump in 1996, the German electronics association ZVEI said on Tuesday.

The unusually cool summer of 1996 sparked a fall-off in sales of German fridges and freezer equipment, leading to an overall three percent shrinking of the market for household electrical goods to 13.4 billion marks, the group said.
Karsten Jaspersen, who heads the ZVEI's consumer electronics division, told a news conference that the expected upturn in demand next year would be fuelled by cuts in personal taxes.
In 1996, output in the sector dropped one percent to 15 billion marks and jobs fell by 5,000 to 60,000.
Jaspersen said the loss of jobs was partly due to excessively high wage agreements in Germany and said German firms needed to improve their productivity to avoid being swamped by foreign competition.
